## GitHub Copilot Commands and OpenSpec Skills

OpenSpec names each workflow by its Agent Skill, while the command a developer types depends on the agent harness running it.  This section covers GitHub Copilot inside VS Code, IntelliJ IDEA, and GitHub Copilot CLI.  VS Code and IntelliJ IDEA use GitHub Copilot's prompt-file integration.  Because GitHub Copilot CLI does not read `.github/prompts/`, the installed skills are the appropriate option there.[^appendix-b-1]

[^appendix-b-1]: [OpenSpec supported tools](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools).  The page documents the GitHub Copilot integration, its `.github/skills/` and `.github/prompts/` locations, the `/openspec-apply-change` skill spelling, the `/opsx-apply` command spelling, and the note that Copilot CLI does not read `.github/prompts/`.

The appropriate integration can install the relevant files when you initialize the repository, for example with `openspec init --tools github-copilot`.[^appendix-b-2]  The table uses the current OPSX command form for the Copilot extensions and the Agent Skill form for Copilot CLI.  OpenSpec documents the command pattern using the apply workflow; the other workflows appear to follow the same host-specific naming pattern.[^appendix-b-3]

[^appendix-b-2]: [OpenSpec CLI reference](https://openspec.dev/docs/cli).  The `init` command accepts a `--tools` option for selecting integrations.

[^appendix-b-3]: [OpenSpec supported tools](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools).  The page documents the GitHub Copilot integration, its `.github/skills/` and `.github/prompts/` locations, the `/openspec-apply-change` skill spelling, the `/opsx-apply` command spelling, and the note that Copilot CLI does not read `.github/prompts/`.

| OpenSpec action | When to use it | VS Code | IntelliJ IDEA | GitHub Copilot CLI |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| `explore` | Investigate an idea, existing behavior, or an unclear requirement before creating a change proposal.  It is a thinking step and does not implement code. | `/opsx-explore <Topic>` | `/opsx-explore <Topic>` | `/openspec-explore <Topic>` |
| `propose` | Turn the agreed problem into a change proposal and generate its planning artifacts. | `/opsx-propose <change-name>` | `/opsx-propose <change-name>` | `/openspec-propose <change-name>` |
| `apply` | Implement the tasks in an existing proposal after reviewing its requirements and design. | `/opsx-apply <change-name>` | `/opsx-apply <change-name>` | `/openspec-apply-change <change-name>` |
| `sync` | Merge implemented delta requirements into `openspec/specs/` while leaving the change proposal open.  Use this when the specification is ready to become the current baseline but the change still needs follow-up work. | `/opsx-sync <change-name>` | `/opsx-sync <change-name>` | `/openspec-sync-specs <change-name>` |
| `archive` | Complete a finished change.  This merges its deltas into the main specs and moves the change folder into `openspec/changes/archive/`. | `/opsx-archive <change-name>` | `/opsx-archive <change-name>` | `/openspec-archive-change <change-name>` |

### Using the matrix

The VS Code and IntelliJ IDEA entries match because both use the GitHub Copilot IDE integration.  OpenSpec generates prompt files under `.github/prompts/`, which the Copilot extension can expose as slash commands in both editors.[^appendix-b-4]

[^appendix-b-4]: [OpenSpec supported tools](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools).  The page documents the GitHub Copilot integration, its `.github/skills/` and `.github/prompts/` locations, the `/openspec-apply-change` skill spelling, the `/opsx-apply` command spelling, and the note that Copilot CLI does not read `.github/prompts/`.

GitHub Copilot CLI uses the skill spelling.  For example, the CLI equivalent of `/opsx-apply pets-search` would be `/openspec-apply-change pets-search`.  The IDE command is not expected to resolve in the CLI because the CLI does not read `.github/prompts/`.[^appendix-b-5]

[^appendix-b-5]: [OpenSpec supported tools](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools).  The page documents the GitHub Copilot integration, its `.github/skills/` and `.github/prompts/` locations, the `/openspec-apply-change` skill spelling, the `/opsx-apply` command spelling, and the note that Copilot CLI does not read `.github/prompts/`.

You might use the rows as a working loop rather than as mandatory ceremony for every small edit.  Explore can help when the problem or existing behavior is unclear.  Propose fits once the intended change is understood well enough to record.  Apply is available when the proposal is ready to execute.  Sync can update the main specification while the change remains open.  Archive generally follows verification and completion, when the change is ready to leave the active-work area and its deltas can become part of the lasting specs.[^appendix-b-6]

[^appendix-b-6]: [OpenSpec skills reference](https://openspec.dev/docs/skills) and [OpenSpec quickstart](https://openspec.dev/docs/quickstart).  These pages define the explore, propose, apply, sync, and archive workflows and their skill names.

The terminal CLI is a separate interface.  Commands such as `openspec init` and `openspec validate` can manage the project and its artifacts from a shell.  Slash commands and skills ask an AI coding tool to carry out a workflow using those artifacts.  If a workflow is unavailable, it may help to check that the repository is initialized and valid and that the selected host can see the files it expects.
